long_biography.plain_text:
Gary Widdowson and his wife, Beverley, turned down substantial offers for Big Star after the London Olympics. Their horse had carried Nick Skelton to team gold in 2012, and keeping him preserved a partnership rooted in Widdowson and Skelton’s friendship as junior riders. Skelton went on to win individual gold with Big Star at Rio in 2016.

Kelling, the North Norfolk estate Widdowson bought, combines holiday cottages and long-term residential lettings with arable farming and conservation. Its woodland programme includes planting trees and hedgerows. Among the estate’s cottages is Big Star, named after the horse.

April 1958 is directly published; the exact birth day and birthplace remain unverified. A London business association is not proof of birth there. No secondary nationality, useful title/suffix or secondary residence is proposed; existing birth country and Alive values are preserved.

The current official controller entries state Barbados. Some older officer appointments still show United Kingdom; a UK company office or property holding is not treated as current main residence. Street addresses are neither proposed nor retained.

The original business was Albert's. Gary's role and family wealth do not prove the mechanism by which he acquired his own stake. Neither inheritance nor self-made status is presumed, and the later estate purchase cannot settle the original mechanism.

Published accounts differ over the exact year of the Barclays transaction, and some mention retained interests. Neither a precise sale year, sale price nor a complete cash exit is asserted. The older Metal & Waste business is not presented as currently Gary's operation.
